what: A future change could let a saved search quietly match far more trials than it asks for, and no check would turn red. The build removed the only note saying why the registry-code check must stay strict. The comment was just above CODE in ctgov.py: "A registry code is a bare word: letters, digits and underscores. Anything else cannot be one, and must not be interpolated into a filter expression -- a stray bracket would close the AREA clause early and leave the rest of the expression to be read as a separate condition, which *widens* the search. Queries are stored as JSON and re-run for months, so this is checked at the point of use rather than trusted to whatever assembled the query." No test, name, docstring or note holds this fact. I loosened CODE to accept anything in a throwaway copy, and all 807 unit tests still passed. The API passes phase, sponsor type and status from the browser straight through, so this check is the only guard.

A future change could make every full recheck store a fresh copy of each trial, even when nothing changed, and no check would turn red. The build removed the note that explains why a full recheck that finds nothing stores nothing. The comment was just above `if revised or moved:` in monitor.check: "A forced check that found nothing has re-fetched the record the baseline already holds, so there is nothing new to keep. Storing it anyway would grow a snapshot per forced check and, worse, advance the stored registry stamp past the change the watchlist is still reporting." The function's docstring does not say this. I changed the condition to always store in a throwaway copy, and all 807 unit tests still passed.
where: monitor.py:834 (check: if revised or moved: storage.add_snapshot)

what: A future change could bring trials the analyst took off every list back onto a new default list after all lists are deleted, and no check would turn red. The build removed the note that explains why the default list leaves those trials out. The comment was in _house_every_trial in storage.py: "Only ever the trials of a database that had no lists at all. A trial that loses its last list while the app is running is deliberately dropped, and re-homing it here would quietly undo that. Not a trial left unwatched on purpose: its removal is recorded and stays." The docstring says the step gives a database with no lists one list "holding everything it has", which reads as the opposite. I deleted the 'stopped' filter in a throwaway copy, and all 807 unit tests still passed. A script then showed the effect: after a trial's only list was deleted and the database reopened, the trial was back on "My watchlist".
where: storage.py:181 (_house_every_trial, WHERE nct_id NOT IN ... kind = 'stopped')

what: A future change could show an undo listed before the review it undid when both happen in the same second, and no check would turn red. The build removed the note that explains the tie order in a trial's history. The comment was just above the order dict in monitor.py: "Newest first; on a tie the later-made kind (undo after review) leads." I swapped the places of review and undo in a throwaway copy, and all 807 unit tests still passed.
where: monitor.py:1203 (the order dict in the trial's history)

what: A future change could make focus jump to the wrong place when a dialog closes, and nothing would explain why the delay is there. The build removed the two notes that explain how a dialog hands focus back. The comments were in the close handler of webapp/static/views/dialog.js: "// The opener may have been redrawn meanwhile: find its replacement by id." and "// After the browser's own focus restore, which would otherwise win." I made the focus immediate in a throwaway copy, and all 227 walks still passed in a quick run. So no check holds the reason, and I do not know whether the delay still matters in today's browsers.

A future change could drop the early focus check and nothing would say what it was for. The build removed the note that gives the reason for the 60 ms timer in webapp/static/focus.js: "// a disabled control loses focus a moment after the change". I removed the timer in a throwaway copy, and all walks still passed, because the later 400 ms check still runs. So losing it may only delay the fix-up, which I did not measure.

The app still carries settings for a date column, a typed date box and shared column widths that no page has. The removed comments show the code is out of date, and the build removed them without removing the code. The comments were "A momentJS pattern, applied client-side by the date column" above DATE_FORMAT, "How a date box is typed into…" above INPUT_DATE_FORMAT, and "How wide each shared column is dealt. Named widths rather than a UI library's column objects, so both pages lay the same columns out the same way." above COLUMN_WIDTHS. I searched the code: INPUT_DATE_FORMAT and COLUMN_WIDTHS are used nowhere, and DATE_FORMAT only by tests/test_display.py. Some functions in display.py are used only inside it (field_line, group_fields, render_card, search_line, study_line), which suggests more of it is left over from the old interface; I did not trace each one.
